hook_text: The water in your glass was brown river mud a few days ago. Not one chemical reaction was needed to clean it. Just four tricks of difference.
clip_script: After a storm the river is brown: sticks, leaves, sand, mud, dissolved salts and germs. Every separation trick uses one idea: find what is different and use it. Different size? Screens catch the sticks and plastic. Different density? A chemical makes the fine mud clump into flakes that sink, and the clear water is poured off the top. Still different size? Deep sand beds filter out the last fine bits. Germs are too small to filter, so a little chlorine kills them. Then it is piped to your tap. The same tricks run the lab. A filter keeps sand as the residue and lets water through as the filtrate. Salt dissolves, so it slips through any filter, but boil the water off and the salt stays behind; catch the steam in a cold tube and you get pure water back. That is distillation. Diamonds? They stick to grease while rock washes away. Mixtures are never chemically joined, so all you need is a difference.
visual_style: A whiteboard river turning from brown to clear through four labelled stages: screen, settling tank, sand filter, chlorine; then a filter funnel with residue and filtrate labelled.
pacing: A steady four-stage journey, then a quick lab montage, ending on the one-rule line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and plan the separation of any mixture.
